analysis.summary: Kubernetes v1.37.0-alpha.1 是一个早期测试版本，主要包含多项API变更、功能废弃、重要Bug修复和性能改进，重点关注kubelet配置修复、API清理和调度器优化。
key_changes: 紧急修复：kubelet配置eventRecordQPS=0的行为变更，现在0表示无限制（之前被当作默认值50） - [PR #117119](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117119) - **影响：** 如果配置中设置了eventRecordQPS=0且希望保持之前的行为，需要手动改为50
API变更：将DisruptionMode从枚举改为结构体，并废弃scheduling.k8s.io/v1alpha2 API版本 - [PR #138572](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138572) - **影响：** 升级时需要清理所有v1alpha2对象
功能提升：DRA（动态资源分配）扩展资源功能正式GA - [PR #138488](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138488) - **影响：** 相关API和功能进入稳定状态
API清理：移除未使用的PodStatusResult类型 - [PR #136271](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136271) - **影响：** 内部API清理，不影响用户
CRI API变更：重命名Signal枚举键以避免C++宏冲突 - [PR #139251](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139251) - **影响：** 需要重新编译使用CRI API的组件
important_bugfixes: 修复StatefulSet OnDelete策略不更新CurrentRevision的问题 - [PR #136833](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136833) - **影响：** 影响使用OnDelete更新策略的StatefulSet状态准确性
修复并行Pod管理中maxUnavailable计算错误的问题 - [PR #137666](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137666) - **影响：** 修复v1.35引入的回归问题，确保StatefulSet滚动更新正常进行
恢复通过环境变量传递二进制数据的能力（修复1.34+的回归） - [PR #139168](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139168) - **影响：** 修复Secret中包含非UTF-8数据时容器创建失败的问题
修复CronJob控制器获取已存在Job时空命名空间的问题 - [PR #136920](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136920) - **影响：** 修复CronJob无法正确采用现有Job的问题
修复kubectl drain --disable-eviction --dry-run=server无限挂起的问题 - [PR #137543](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137543) - **影响：** 影响使用dry-run模式的运维操作
修复Windows kube-proxy在IP重用场景下的远程端点清理问题 - [PR #138000](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138000) - **影响：** 解决Windows节点上因IP重用导致的网络连接问题
security_issues: 加强kubelet日志相关端点的HTTP方法限制 - [PR #138088](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138088) - **风险级别：** 低 - 明确限制只读端点仅允许GET方法
修复etcd不安全删除路径的数据损坏问题 - [PR #137582](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137582) - **风险级别：** 中 - 确保数据一致性，防止潜在的数据损坏
performance_improvements: 实现watch cache的RangeStream以提升初始化性能 - [PR #136915](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136915) - **提升：** 通过单次RPC流式传输替代分页请求，减少watch cache初始化时间
优化GangScheduling插件仅在需要时执行 - [PR #135905](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135905) - **提升：** 减少不必要的插件执行，提升调度器性能

多项指标从Alpha提升到Beta稳定性 - [PR #136189](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136189)、[PR #137072](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137072)、[PR #136894](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136894)、[PR #137116](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137116) - **提升：** 提供更稳定的监控指标
breaking_changes: 废弃kubectl run的--filename/-f标志（该标志原本被忽略） - [PR #138671](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138671) - **影响：** 使用该标志将收到废弃警告，需要移除
移除kubeadm v1beta3 API和PublicKeysECDSA特性门控 - [PR #136016](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136016) - **影响：** 需要更新kubeadm配置
移除AnyVolumeDataSource特性门控（功能已稳定） - [PR #135336](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135336) - **影响：** 相关功能默认启用，无需配置特性门控
移除SidecarContainers特性门控（功能已稳定） - [PR #137755](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137755) - **影响：** 相关功能默认启用
清理已废弃的DefaultWatchCacheSize等etcd选项 - [PR #134151](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134151) - **影响：** 需要更新相关配置
recommendations: **重要：** 如果kubelet配置中设置了eventRecordQPS=0，升级前请检查是否需要改为50以保持原有行为
**API迁移：** 如果使用scheduling.k8s.io/v1alpha2 API，升级前需要迁移到v1alpha3并清理v1alpha2对象
**测试建议：** 在测试环境中充分验证StatefulSet滚动更新、CronJob管理和Windows网络功能
**监控更新：** 更新监控仪表板以使用新的Beta指标，确保兼容性
**工具链更新：** 如果使用CRI API开发容器运行时，需要重新编译以适应Signal枚举键的变更
analysis.risk_assessment: 整体风险评估：中等。这是一个alpha版本，包含多个API变更和破坏性变更，不建议在生产环境使用。主要风险包括：1) kubelet配置行为变更可能导致事件记录限制意外变化；2) API版本废弃需要迁移工作；3) Windows网络修复可能影响现有配置。建议仅在测试环境中评估，重点关注StatefulSet、CronJob和Windows节点的功能验证。升级时机：等待beta或稳定版本发布后再考虑生产环境升级。

138671.title: kubectl: deprecate run filename flag
138671.body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind deprecation
#### What this PR does / why we need it:
`kubectl run` registers `--filename/-f` through `DeleteFlags`, but the run command does not consume `FilenameOptions`.
The command still builds the generated Pod from command-line arguments such as `NAME` and `--image`, and ignores the file passed through `--filename/-f`.
This PR starts the deprecation process for `kubectl run --filename/-f`.
#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Follow-up to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138632
#### Special notes for your reviewer:
This follows up on maintainer feedback from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138632#issuecomment-4333274675.
The scope is intentionally limited to `--filename/-f`.
#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Deprecated the ignored `--filename`/`-f` flag on `kubectl run`.
```

  This PR removes the unused `PodStatusResult` type from the Kubernetes API.

  **Background:**
  - `PodStatusResult` was introduced in January 2015 ([PR #3565](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/3565)) as a wrapper type for encoding/decoding pod status returned by kubelet's `/podInfo` endpoint

  - Removing it reduces maintenance burden and codebase complexity

136709.title: DRA: improve CEL error message for "no such key" errors
136709.body:
## What this PR does

This PR improves the error message when CEL selectors access non-existent device attributes. When users write expressions like `device.attributes["gpu.nvidia.com"].sharingStrategy == "runai-fractions"` without checking if the attribute exists first, they currently get a generic "no such key" error with no guidance on how to fix it.

## Why this approach

### String matching for error detection

We detect "no such key" errors using `strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "no such key:")` instead of `errors.Is()` because:
- cel-go's `resolutionError` type is not exported (internal package)
- The cel-go library wraps errors in `types.Err` which only forwards the error message
- Kubernetes itself uses this pattern in apiextensions-apiserver (`staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/schema/cel/validation.go:759`)

### Why these three allocator files

The modification is applied to three allocator variants:
- `structured/internal/stable/allocator_stable.go`
- `structured/internal/incubating/allocator_incubating.go`
- `structured/internal/experimental/allocator_experimental.go`

These three files represent different maturity levels of the DRA allocator implementation. They must be kept in sync because:
1. They are the core CEL selector evaluation points in DRA
2. Features rotate between them as they mature (experimental → incubating → stable)
3. Maintaining consistency ensures behavior is preserved during rotation

### Error message references documentation

The enhanced error message links to `pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/resource/v1#CELDeviceSelector` instead of hardcoding examples. This ensures the error guidance stays current as the CEL documentation evolves with the codebase.

### Documentation improvements

We added concrete examples to `CELDeviceSelector` showing how to handle optional attributes using `orValue()`, `has()`, and the `?` operator. These examples demonstrate the robust patterns users should adopt to avoid "no such key" errors.

## Release note

```release-note
Improved CEL error messages in Dynamic Resource Allocation to provide guidance when accessing non-existent device attributes. Error messages now link to documentation on handling optional fields using orValue() and has().
```

## Related Issue

Fixes #135661

## Test

Added unit tests in `errors_test.go` to verify error enhancement behavior.

138000.title: Delete remote endpoint if it has same ip as local endpoint in the system.
138000.body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

**Handling Stale Remote Endpoints When Local and Remote Endpoints Share the Same IP (getAllEndpointsByNetwork)**

On Windows Server 2019 and Windows Server 2022, within an L2Bridge network configuration, all pods across cluster nodes typically share the same pod subnet.

In scenarios where the subnet range is limited, or even when larger ranges are heavily utilized, IP address reuse can occur. For example, when a pod assigned an IP address (e.g., 10.0.0.1) is deleted, that IP may later be reassigned to a new pod on a different node immediately. In such cases, the CNI creates a new local endpoint for the reused IP.

However, the corresponding remote endpoint associated with the previously deleted pod may not yet have been cleaned up, as it could still be awaiting deletion signals. Because the IP is already reassigned locally, KubeProxy may inadvertently increase the reference count of the stale remote endpoint and delay its removal. This can result in both a local and a remote endpoint coexisting with the same IP address in HNS.

This duplication can lead to unintended behavior. For instance, when a pod using the reused IP attempts DNS resolution, traffic is load-balanced at the host port (particularly in non-DSR mode). After DNAT, the VFP rule may select the MAC address of the remote endpoint instead of the local pod. Since subsequent VFP processing interprets this as traffic destined for a remote endpoint, packets may be encapsulated and routed to an incorrect node rather than the appropriate DNS pod. This can ultimately cause DNS timeouts.

To address this issue, the fix prioritizes local endpoints. When a local endpoint is detected for an IP that also has a remote endpoint, the remote endpoint is marked for deletion and replaced by the local one. Additionally, any stale remote endpoints with duplicate IP addresses are systematically cleaned up using deleteAllRemoteEndpointsWithDupIP at the end of each syncProxyRules() cycle.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Fixes #137381 

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed stale remote HNS endpoint cleanup on Windows when a pod IP is reused across nodes in L2Bridge networks, preventing DNS timeouts caused by traffic being routed to the wrong node.
```

137767.title: Adding prometheues metrics for Kubeproxy failed loadbalancer operations.
137767.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Adds Prometheus metrics for Windows kube-proxy (winkernel) load balancer
operation failures. Previously, the winkernel proxier had no metrics for LB
failures, making it difficult to monitor and diagnose issues in production
Windows clusters.

This PR introduces three new `ALPHA` stability counter metrics:

- `kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_winkernel_lb_create_failures_total` - tracks LB creation failures
- `kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_winkernel_lb_update_failures_total` - tracks LB update failures
- `kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_winkernel_lb_delete_failures_total` - tracks LB deletion failures

Each metric has three labels for fine-grained observability:

- `ip_family` - `IPv4` or `IPv6`
- `lb_type` - `clusterip`, `nodeport`, `externalip`, `ingressip`, or `healthcheck`
- `error`  - `network_not_found`, `port_already_exists`, `not_implemented`, `invalid_ip`, or `other`

The maximum cardinality per metric is 50 (2 × 5 × 5), but in practice is much
lower since a proxier instance uses a single IP family and most error/lb_type
combinations never fire.

**Implementation details:**

- Defines type-safe `loadBalancerType` and `lbErrorType` string typedefs with constants
- Adds a `classifyLBError` function that maps HCN/HNS errors to a finite set of error categories using the hcn package's error classification helpers
- Changes `mapStaleLoadbalancers` from `map[string]bool` to `map[string]loadBalancerType` to preserve the LB type through stale LB cleanup retries
- Threads `lbType` through `deleteExistingLoadBalancer`, `deleteLoadBalancer`, `deleteLoadBalancerPolicy`, and `cleanupAllPolicies`
- Emits metrics at all 8 failure sites (3 create, 3 update, 2 delete paths)
- Registers the new metrics under `ProxyModeKernelspace` in `RegisterMetrics`

**Example metrics from a real AKS Windows node:**

```

TYPE kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_winkernel_lb_create_failures_total counter
kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_winkernel_lb_create_failures_total{error="other",ip_family="IPv4",lb_type="clusterip"} 222
kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_winkernel_lb_create_failures_total{error="port_already_exists",ip_family="IPv4",lb_type="nodeport"} 310
kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_winkernel_lb_create_failures_total{error="port_already_exists",ip_family="IPv6",lb_type="clusterip"} 83
```

```go
clientset, _, tearDownFn := framework.StartTestServer(tCtx, t, framework.TestServerSetup{
```

#### What type of PR is this?


#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When `checkAndDecrement` returns a `Forbidden` error due to negative `DisruptionsAllowed` or an oversized `DisruptedPods` map, clients had no programmatic way to distinguish these from other `Forbidden` errors without string-matching on the message.

This PR adds two new `CauseType` constants to `policy/v1`:
- `DisruptionBudgetNegativeAllowedDisruptions` — for the `DisruptionsAllowed < 0` case
- `DisruptionBudgetTooManyDisruptedPods` — for the `DisruptedPods` map overflow case

And populates `StatusCause` on both `Forbidden` error paths in `checkAndDecrement`, consistent with the existing pattern already used on the `TooManyRequests` path via `DisruptionBudgetCause`.

Clients can now use `errors.HasStatusCause(err, policyv1.DisruptionBudgetNegativeAllowedDisruptions)` for reliable, typed, machine-readable error discrimination, no message parsing needed.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Fixes #125500

#### Special notes:

The two new `CauseType` constants follow the same naming convention and placement as the existing `DisruptionBudgetCause` constant in `staging/src/k8s.io/api/policy/v1/types.go`. No codegen changes were required since `CauseType` is a `string` alias.

```release-note
Added structured `CauseType` values to PodDisruptionBudget-related eviction `Forbidden` errors in the eviction API, allowing clients to programmatically distinguish PDB invalid-state errors from other forbidden errors without string-matching on the message.
```

There should be no limit when the values are set to 0.

135661.title: DRA: Scheduler CEL evaluation fails with "no such key" when accessing nested attributes without existence check
135661.body:
### What happened?

I am using DRA with a CEL selector to filter devices based on driver attributes. When writing an expression that accesses a nested field within `device.attributes`, the scheduler encounters a CEL runtime error if the specific driver key does not exist on the device, rather than evaluating the expression to false.

The following expression fails during the DynamicResources filter plugin execution:

```
cel:
  expression: 'device.attributes["gpu.nvidia.com"].sharingStrategy == "runai-fractions"'
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected the expression to evaluate to false for devices that do not possess the gpu.nvidia.com attribute, allowing the scheduler to simply skip those devices.

Instead, the scheduler treats this as a hard runtime error, preventing the claim from being allocated even if valid devices exist, or logging significant errors during the filter phase.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: DeviceClass
metadata:
  name: gpu.nvidia.com
spec:
  selectors:
  - cel: 
      expression: "device.driver == 'gpu.nvidia.com'"
---
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceSlice
metadata:
  name: kind-control-plane-gpu-devices-slice
spec:
  nodeName: kind-control-plane
  driver: gpu.nvidia.com

  pool:
    generation: 1
    resourceSliceCount: 1
    name: kind-control-plane-gpu-pool

  devices:
  - name: gpu-0
    bindsToNode: true

  - name: gpu-1
    attributes:
      sharingStrategy:
        string: runai-fractions
    bindsToNode: true
---
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceClaim
metadata:
  name: kind-control-plane-gpu-runai-fractionable-claim-1
spec:
  devices:
    requests:
    - name: gpu-runai-fractionable
      exactly:
        deviceClassName: gpu.nvidia.com
        capacity:
          requests:
            memory: 10Gi
        selectors:
        - cel:
            expression: 'device.attributes["gpu.nvidia.com"].sharingStrategy == "runai-fractions"'
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: fraction-pod-1
spec:
  resourceClaims:
  - name: fraction-claim
    resourceClaimName: kind-control-plane-gpu-runai-fractionable-claim-1
  containers:
  - name: fraction-container
    resources:
      claims:
      - name: fraction-claim
    image: ubuntu:latest
    command: [ "/bin/bash", "-c", "--" ]
    args: [sleep Infinity"]
```

```
> kubectl describe pod fraction-pod-1
...
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age              From               Message
  ----     ------            ----             ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  3s               default-scheduler  0/1 nodes are available: 1 cannot allocate all claims. still not schedulable, preemption: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.
```

In release 1.36, we introduced initial changes to the Workload API (including `Workload` and `PodGroup` objects) in the `v1alpha2` version of the `scheduling.k8s.io` API group. For the 1.37 release, we plan to make further changes to these APIs and eventually promote them to Beta.

We will migrate all internal consumers to `v1alpha3` and remove `v1alpha2` in this release. This avoids the overhead of maintaining both versions with conversion logic for an experimental API, while allowing us to evolve the API.

We would like to promote the Workload API to `v1alpha3` and remove `v1alpha2` by performing the following steps:
1.  **Create `v1alpha3` API Definitions**:

    *   Copy `pkg/apis/scheduling/v1alpha2` to `v1alpha3`.
    *   Update package names and references to point to the new `v1alpha3`.
2.  **Remove `v1alpha2` API Definitions**:
    *   Delete the old `v1alpha2` directories in both `staging` and `pkg/apis`.
3.  **Update Internal References**:
    *   Update all imports and usages of `k8s.io/api/scheduling/v1alpha2` to `v1alpha3` across the repository (e.g., in `pkg/scheduler/`, `plugin/pkg/admission/`).

139132.title: CreateContainerError when secret env var contains invalid UTF-8 bytes (gRPC strict validation regression)
139132.body:
### What happened?

Pods fail with `CreateContainerError` and the following event (events.k8s.io/v1) message:

```
Error: grpc: error while marshaling: string field contains invalid UTF-8
```

When an environment variable sourced from a Kubernetes Secret contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8. The kubelet passes the raw secret bytes as a protobuf `string` field in the CRI `CreateContainerRequest` to containerd. Since gRPC v1.72+ (bundled in k8s 1.34) enforces strict UTF-8 validation on `string` fields, the container creation is rejected.

This is distinct from #136323 / #136325 which fixed env var *expansion* truncating multi-byte UTF-8 characters. That fix does not address this case - here the secret value itself contains raw bytes that were never valid UTF-8 in the first place.

The same pods work on kubelet v1.33.7 nodes in the same cluster because the older gRPC version did not enforce UTF-8 validation on string fields. This is a silent behavioral regression with no warning or migration path.

### What did you expect to happen?

Either:

1. The kubelet should validate secret values for UTF-8 correctness before sending them over CRI gRPC, and emit a clear warning/event identifying which env var contains the invalid value.
2. The CRI protobuf definition should use `bytes` instead of `string` for env var values (since secrets are fundamentally binary).
3. At minimum, the error message should identify which specific environment variable contains the invalid UTF-8, rather than the opaque gRPC marshaling error.

Currently there is no indication of which env var is problematic, making debugging difficult.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```bash
# 1. Create a secret containing invalid UTF-8 bytes
#    \xc3\x28 is an incomplete UTF-8 sequence (0xC3 expects a continuation byte 0x80-0xBF, not 0x28)
python3 -c "
import base64
invalid_bytes = b'hello\xc3\x28world'
encoded = base64.b64encode(invalid_bytes).decode()
manifest = f'''apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: utf8-invalid-secret
  namespace: default
data:
  test-key: {encoded}
'''
print(manifest)
" | kubectl apply -f -

# 2. Create a pod that uses this secret as an env var
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: utf8-test-invalid
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - name: test
    image: busybox:latest
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
    env:
    - name: BAD_VAR
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: utf8-invalid-secret
          key: test-key
  restartPolicy: Never
EOF

# 3. Observe the pod enters CreateContainerError
kubectl get pod utf8-test-invalid
# NAME                READY   STATUS                 RESTARTS   AGE
# utf8-test-invalid   0/1     CreateContainerError   0          14s

kubectl describe pod utf8-test-invalid | grep -A2 "Warning.*Failed"
# Warning  Failed  kubelet  Error: grpc: error while marshaling: string field contains invalid UTF-8
```

Note: The same secret and pod spec works without error on k8s 1.33 nodes (older gRPC without strict UTF-8 enforcement).

120181.body:
### What happened?

We have a custom resource with a name - `Foo`
We have a CronJob named - `Foo`

Now, we have a job whose owner refernce is set to the custom resource name - `Foo`. We have noticed that the job when stopped (suspended) basically causes an event/warning - "[UnexpectedJob](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8b132ea40a250e9acf08ab2fadb9a8c2fd811d74/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L444C39-L444C55)" for the given job execution.

[syncCronJob](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8b132ea40a250e9acf08ab2fadb9a8c2fd811d74/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L422C25-L422C36) is trying to reconcile the job because it thinks that it is owned by the CronJob. Probably because of "[getJobsToBeReconciled](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8b132ea40a250e9acf08ab2fadb9a8c2fd811d74/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L252C25-L252C46)", at this [line](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8b132ea40a250e9acf08ab2fadb9a8c2fd811d74/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L264C3-L264C110).

### What did you expect to happen?

The `syncCronJob` should not try to reconcile the job because it is not owned by the CronJob.

The `getJobsToBeReconciled` method should match the `name` and the `kind` of the job. The `kind` in the case of a cronjob would be `CronJob`.

- Run a job execution using the same CRD used to create a cronjob.
- Once the job execution starts, stop (suspend) it.
- We would start getting events of type `Warning` with reason - `UnexpectedJob`.

### What would you like to be added?

When multiple StorageClasses are annotated as default (`storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true"`), Kubernetes uses the most recently created one as the actual default applied to PVCs without an explicit storageClassName.

136831.title: StatefulSet function completeRollingUpdate does not check AvailableReplicas (minReadySeconds bug)
136831.body:
### What happened?

When a StatefulSet has `minReadySeconds` configured, the `completeRollingUpdate` function prematurely marks the rolling update as complete. It sets `status.CurrentRevision = status.UpdateRevision` as soon as all replicas are Ready, without waiting for them to be Available (i.e., Ready for at least `minReadySeconds`).

### What did you expect to happen?

The rolling update should not be considered complete until all replicas are both Ready and Available (have been Ready for at least minReadySeconds).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a StatefulSet with minReadySeconds set to a non-zero value (e.g., 60s)
2. Trigger a rolling update
3. Observe that status.CurrentRevision is updated to status.UpdateRevision before pods have been Available for at least minReadySeconds

### Anything else we need to know?

Root cause:

In function [completeRollingUpdate](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.35.0/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set_utils.go#L638-L647), the condition checks ReadyReplicas but not AvailableReplicas:

```go
func completeRollingUpdate(set *apps.StatefulSet, status *apps.StatefulSetStatus) {
	if set.Spec.UpdateStrategy.Type == apps.RollingUpdateStatefulSetStrategyType &&
		status.UpdatedReplicas == *set.Spec.Replicas &&
		status.ReadyReplicas == *set.Spec.Replicas &&
		status.Replicas == *set.Spec.Replicas {
		status.CurrentReplicas = status.UpdatedReplicas
		status.CurrentRevision = status.UpdateRevision
	}
}
```


The fix is to add status.AvailableReplicas == *set.Spec.Replicas to the condition. This was originally identified in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122272#discussion_r1526750533.

Kubernetes version: all versions since StatefulSetMinReadySeconds graduated to GA (v1.27+)

### What happened?

I decided to open this issue after investigating https://github.com/stackabletech/trino-operator/issues/854.

This doesn't happen if the `MaxUnavailableStatefulSet` feature is disabled.

137766.title: Add Prometheus metrics for Windows kube-proxy (winkernel) load balancer failures
137766.body:
### What would you like to be added?

The Windows kube-proxy (winkernel proxier) currently lacks Prometheus metrics for load balancer operation failures. This makes it difficult to monitor and diagnose LB failures in production Windows clusters.

**Proposed metrics:**

Add three new `ALPHA` stability counter metrics:
- `kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_winkernel_lb_create_failures_total` - tracks LB creation failures
- `kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_winkernel_lb_update_failures_total` - tracks LB update failures  
- `kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_winkernel_lb_delete_failures_total` - tracks LB deletion failures

**Proposed labels for each metric:**

| Label | Values |
|-------|--------|
| `ip_family` | `IPv4`, `IPv6` |
| `lb_type` | `clusterip`, `nodeport`, `externalip`, `ingressip`, `healthcheck` |
| `error` | `network_not_found`, `port_already_exists`, `not_implemented`, `invalid_ip`, `other` |

The maximum cardinality per metric would be 50 (2 × 5 × 5), but in practice much lower since a proxier instance typically uses a single IP family and most error/lb_type combinations never fire.

### Why is this needed?

1. **Observability gap**: Linux kube-proxy modes (iptables, ipvs, nftables) have extensive metrics, but Windows winkernel proxier has none for LB failures.
2. **Production debugging**: Without these metrics, operators have no visibility into HCN/HNS failures until services become unavailable.
3. **Alerting**: Cannot set up proactive alerting on LB failure rates in Windows clusters.
4. **Parity**: Brings Windows kube-proxy closer to feature parity with Linux modes in terms of observability.

### Additional context

Example output from a real AKS Windows node:


  - Rapid CSV reconciliation for servicemeshoperator3.v3.2.0 and kiali-operator.v2.17.2

  The getEventKey function in events_cache.go constructs an event key by joining multiple fields:

```go
  The `getEventKey` function in `events_cache.go` constructs an event key by joining multiple fields:
```
